Issue #498 in re-cinq/Otto: Stop the tool-budget message promising a follow-up while no escalation destination exists
State: open
Author: saadahmed95
Labels: size:S, area:compliance, epic:E4, repo:otto, type:bug, priority:medium, lore:blocked
Opened: 2026-10-23T19:09:53Z
Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/Otto/issues/498

> **Blocked:** a decision on what the message may promise while no escalation destination exists (KU-14), and a Danish speaker for any new wording (KU-15). Nothing to implement until then.

## Why

`TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA` (#151, shipped in #439) ends with "En kollega vil følge op på din henvendelse.", a colleague will follow up. The agent shows it when the tool budget runs out, and records a `tool_budget_exhausted` escalation.

## What to do

- `apps/api/src/budget/budgetMessage.ts` (new): exports `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA`, a single Danish string constant that promises nothing concrete (no channel, time, or person) and carries no persona name.
- `apps/api/src/budget/budgetHooks.ts` (new): exports `budgetHooks: Partial<OrchestratorHooks>`, whose `onToolBudgetExhausted` fragment calls `escalationRecorder.mark(session.sessionId, 'tool_budget_exhausted')` then returns `TOOL_BUDGET_MESSAGE_DA`. The string renders in the assistant's own bubble (via the normal `entry_upsert` → `entry_delta` → `entry_commit` text path), not through `117`'s catalogue - it is first person, the opposite of `117`'s impersonal wording, because it appears to speak as the assistant rather than as a system alert.
- `apps/api/src/escalation/trigge…

## Why

With no escalation destination configured, nobody is notified. The escalation spec's first paragraph and FR-015 say so: the record stays at `no_destination_configured`. The re:cinq test environment runs exactly that way, because `deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml` sets no `escalationWebhookSecretName` while KU-14 is open. So the message promises a follow-up that nobody is told to make. With testers that is harmless. With a real customer it is a broken promise that reads as service.

FR-017 forbids a phone number, email, opening hour, `ring`, `minutter`, `timer` and a persona name, but not a promised follow-up, so its test passes.

The same question blocks #460's FR-013 and FR-014, a hand-off sentence promising that OLT will contact the customer. See the review on #478.

Widen `ChatMessageList`'s `entries` to `ReadonlyArray<UserChatEntry | AssistantChatEntry | ToolChatEntry>` (not the full `ChatEntry` union - thinking entries stay unrendered until `087`), dispatch on `role`, and forward `describeTool`, `showToolName`, `showToolInput` and `toolIcon` unchanged, the same pass-through shape `028` already uses. ## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **GDPR.** The `warn` log line carries exactly `sessionId`, `maxToolRounds`, and `requestedTools` (tool names only) and nothing else - a test with a user message containing a name and phone number and a tool input containing a booking reference asserts neither appears in any logged argument, and no key named `toolInput` appears
- [ ] **GDPR.** `054`'s five-field `toEqual` assertion over the whole escalation document still passes with this trigger, confirming `requestedTools` never reaches the collection
- [ ] The string is Danish, promises nothing (no phone number, email, opening hour, or the words `ring`, `minutter`, `timer`), and carries no persona name

# Support agent escalation

## User Scenarios & Testing

### User Story 3 - The customer is told when the tool budget runs out (Priority: P1, #151)

A customer asks a question that makes the model keep requesting tools until the budget runs out. Instead of an empty bubble, the assistant replies with one Danish sentence that promises nothing it cannot keep, and an escalation is recorded. A broken hook fragment on this path does not break the turn.

**Why this priority:** An empty reply is the worst outcome for a support channel, and this is the only turn ending with no owner.

**Independent Test:** Run the engine with `maxToolRounds: 2` and a stub that always requests tools. Assert one escalation document containing `tool_budget_exhausted` and the sentence in the committed assistant entry. …
